gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Club Car Precedent (2004 to present) has an On-Board Computer that runs lead-acid charging, which ROYPOW says 'is incompatible with lithium chemistry' and must be bypassed with a harness, a step its guide calls 'mandatory on most 48V Club Car models'.
standout_why: I fully read two of the ten result pages: Golf Cart Gear Lab's 2026-11-11 roundup and our own dealectric.com page. Golf Cart Gear Lab gives BMS amps for each pack and a general line that a flooded lead-acid charger 'will not charge LiFePO4 correctly'. It says nothing about the Club Car OBC, regen braking or precharge. Our page covers BMS burst windows, controller draw and regen in the cold, but it also never mentions the OBC. The two LiTime pages ChatGPT cited returned HTTP 429, and the Gearranking hub failed with an SSL error, so I could not read them. I did not open Cartvolts or Golf Cart Showdown. 'None of the rivals has it' is confirmed for 2 of the 10 pages, not all of them.
decides: This confirms the shortlist and adds a condition to it rather than changing the order. Club Car is the first cart ChatGPT named. On a Precedent, a battery-only budget pick (LiTime 48V 100Ah at about $900, or Redodo, where ChatGPT says to 'check whether a compatible charger is included') still needs a lithium charger plus an OBC bypass before it will charge properly. Its sticker price is therefore not the real conversion cost. A Club Car-specific kit with a dedicated charger, such as Vatrer's at $1,579.99, avoids buying a charger separately, but I could not confirm that any kit includes the bypass harness. The current mechanism ChatGPT raised (BMS continuous amps against controller draw) stays an open check. LiTime's 100 A continuous rating is already noted by ChatGPT and our page, and I could not source stock controller ratings from Curtis or Club Car.

findings.label: Club Car models with an On-Board Computer (OBC)
findings.value: Club Car Precedent, 2004 to present: 'The Precedent also features an On-Board Computer (OBC) that manages lead-acid charging.'
findings.source_title: Club Car Lithium Conversion Guide: Everything You Need Before You Buy (ROYPOW blog, 24 Jun 2026)
findings.note: ROYPOW makes lithium golf cart batteries, so this is a maker's guide, not Club Car's own documentation. Its checklist also mentions 'later DS models', but its DS section never mentions an OBC.

findings.label: Why the OBC has to be bypassed for lithium
findings.value: The OBC's charging profile 'is incompatible with lithium chemistry'. A bypass harness hands charge management to the battery's own BMS, and the guide calls the bypass 'mandatory on most 48V Club Car models'.
findings.source_title: Club Car Lithium Conversion Guide: Everything You Need Before You Buy (ROYPOW blog, 24 Jun 2026)
findings.note: The page does not say what fails if the bypass is skipped (charger lockout, pack drain or a no-run cart). It does warn that lead-acid chargers 'can overcharge lithium cells and trigger BMS lockout or permanent cell damage'.
